_comment: Goals conceded WHILE ON THE PITCH, as a table of cases both languages read.
app.js and daily_pull.py each implement this, because each is a writer and a
stat that two writers disagree about is exactly the bug this replaces. Two
implementations need one specification, so it lives here rather than being
written out twice and drifting the first time somebody fixes only one.
THE WINDOW RULE, which every case below is an instance of: a goal counts
against a player when start < minute <= end. A starter has start 0, so every
goal from the first minute counts. A substitute has start = the minute he came
on, and the man he replaced has end = that same minute -- so a goal in the
minute of a substitution belongs to exactly one of them, never both and never
END = 100000 stands for 'was still on at the final whistle'. A literal 90
would drop stoppage-time goals, which is the half of the match this rule is

cases.name: a starter who plays the full match carries the lot
a starter substituted off is not charged for what happened after
a substitute brought on with the game already lost is charged nothing
cases._note: conceded 0, but no clean sheet either -- he played 20 minutes, and the 60-minute floor is a separate condition that this rule does not touch.

cases.name: a goal in the minute of the substitution belongs to the man going off
a substitute who is himself substituted has both ends
cases._note: The case the free approximation gets wrong: 40 minutes played, and 'the last 40 minutes' would be 50-90, charging him the 85th-minute goal he was not there for.

cases.name: a player sent off stops being charged when he leaves
cases._note: He is punished for the red card by the card rule. Charging him for goals conceded after he had left the field would be the same unfairness this whole change removes.

cases.name: a second yellow is a red
an own goal is charged to the side that scored it
cases._note: API-Football files an own goal under the team of the player who put it in. Read naively that is backwards -- it would credit the concession to the side that benefited.

cases.name: a missed penalty is not a goal
cases._note: API-Football files a missed penalty as type Goal. Read naively it concedes one.

cases.name: a clean sheet needs the hour as well as the shut-out
cases._note: Nothing conceded while he was on, but 55 minutes is short of the hour, so no clean sheet. The two conditions are independent and both have to hold.

cases.name: off at the hour of a goalless game that is later lost
cases._note: The visible consequence of the change: he KEEPS the clean sheet his side lost after he had gone off. Under the old whole-match rule he lost it.

_comment: When the events cannot say where a player was, the club's whole-match total
is used -- which is the behaviour being replaced, and the right thing to fall
back to. Charging nobody because nobody could be placed would silently
under-score a matchday and look identical to a clean sheet.
unplaceable._note: A substitute with no substitution event naming him. He cannot be placed, so he is charged what his club let in.

no_events._comment: No events at all -- an older match, or a feed gap. Everyone gets the club total, exactly as before this rule existed.
